Kill switch, steps 4 and 5 of the desktop plan - the switch, the way out, and the block kept while disconnected. The Kill Switch page on Windows and Linux is a switch page with a note on the way out under it, and under the switch, while it is on, an option to keep the block while disconnected (UserSettings.KillSwitchLockdown, off by default: a hotel's Wi-Fi sign-in needs it off). Settings shows the kill switch's state with the premium crown; while the block is up with no session (AppState.IsKillSwitchBlocking, read from the OS at the app's start, at each session's end and after each change of the app's own, never per state read), a bar in the reconnect bar's place says "The kill switch is blocking the internet." with Disconnect, or under the option, Turn off, which opens the page; the tray's tooltip says it and its Disconnect is enabled; `vhclient status` prints "Kill switch: blocking the internet". The option's block is put up by the settings' split (VpnKillSwitchRules.CreateBySettings, shared with the service's connect) at a person's disconnect, when the option is turned on and at the app's start, and lifted by turning it or the switch off; `vhclient kill-switch lockdown on|off`. The way out, for a service or an exe that will not run: a script in the install - Windows PowerShell 5.1 removing the WFP filters by Add-Type, asking for UAC itself, behind a Start-menu entry "<product> - Turn off kill switch"; a shell script beside Linux's launcher behind a "Turn off kill switch" right-click action - which `vhclient kill-switch off` runs where the service is not running (Linux: root's, else "Try: sudo vhclient kill-switch off"), and both uninstallers run after the service is gone; both lift any VpnHood app's block. AppFeatures carries the Linux script's path for the page's command; Windows' page names the Start-menu entry. The words are in Assets.Classic Tested: on the Windows Server 2025 Desktop and Ubuntu 26.04 VMs against the server VM - the setups place the script and its entry; after a crash, status and the probes show the block; `kill-switch off` with the service stopped lifts it (Ubuntu: refused as a person, done with sudo); the option blocks at once, stays after a disconnect and through a reboot (Ubuntu's boot unit before network-pre.target, the service putting it back after boot), and is lifted by turning it or the switch off; the script works with the app's version folder gone; an uninstall while blocked leaves no filter, table, boot copy, unit, entry or service. Found: with no session, the option blocks the LAN too unless Split Local Network is on, and the replies to inbound connections, so SSH into such a box needs that split.
